description: BatchNorm backward (spatial mode, saved mean and inverse variance from the forward pass) in the HIP_MLOPS_ENGINE region: rank 4 or 5, NCHW/NCDHW or NHWC/NDHWC strides, float/half/bfloat16 x, dy and dx with float scale, dscale, dbias and statistics (the backward kernels use a single fp_type for x, dy and dx, BatchNormBwdSpatial.cpp:837-839, although the applicability check would accept differing io dtypes, BatchnormApplicabilityChecks.cpp:65-76), N*H*W > 1, hw and n swept around the kernel-variant thresholds (hw 60/200/512/1024/4096, n 32/64/768) and powers of two +-1. Template: quick BatchnormBackward/Variant2 (saved mean and inv-variance, the full backward tensor set; Default recomputes the statistics and sets no mean/inv-variance). The tuned input ranges of the quick sweep are copied: inv_variance 1.9..2.0 stays positive, as an rsqrt output must. The axis domain (default/narrow/wide/positive/constant/nonzero/zeros/large/subnormal/nan/inf) renders the fills of x (uid 7) and dy (uid 3) in metadata.inputs; default keeps the quick sweep's x -1..1 and dy -0.1..0.1, the other finite domains use the shared table for both; large keeps scale 32 (worst-case half dx stays near 1e4, below 65504, because scale*inv_variance <= 0.2); scale, mean and inv_variance keep their tuned literal ranges. For nan and inf, x and dy stay at their default ranges (a non-finite x or dy element spreads through the channel sums to all of dscale, dbias and dx of its channel) and the special fill (5% of elements, at least one) goes on scale (uid 6): it only multiplies dx, so dscale and dbias stay finite and only the poisoned channels of dx are non-finite; c == 1 would make all of dx non-finite, and match_nonfinite fails a reference with no finite element, so a constraint rejects nan and inf at c == 1. Further constraints keep the oracle inside what it can grade: half and bfloat16 with the wide, positive and large domains, whose dx is far larger than the sub-ulp half and bfloat16 backward tolerances can grade; and bounds on n*hw (2**15 for constant, 2**21 for positive, 2**11 for wide and large) beyond which the sequential fp32 CPU reference sums of dscale and dbias stagnate or carry more rounding noise than the 2e-3 tolerance (see each constraint's reason). The validator is match_nonfinite exactly for nan and inf. The last axes, alignment (1..256) and placement (default/exact/under), declare that alignment on every device tensor (tensor_patches on uids 0-7) and place the run's pointers accordingly; under misaligns x (placement_uid 7) and needs alignment >= 2, so eff_placement turns under into exact at alignment 1.

derive.d: ds if ndim == 5 and (hw // h) % ds == 0 else 1
derive.dims_x: [n, c, h, w] if ndim == 4 else [n, c, d, h, w]
derive.xs_h: w if layout == 'nchw' else w * c
derive.xs_d: h * w if layout == 'nchw' else h * w * c
derive.xs_c: d * h * w if layout == 'nchw' else 1
derive.stride_x: [xs_n, xs_c, xs_h, xs_w] if ndim == 4 else [xs_n, xs_c, xs_d, xs_h, xs_w]
derive.stride_s: [c, 1, ss_w, ss_w] if ndim == 4 else [c, 1, ss_w, ss_w, ss_w]
derive.dom_kind: 'fixed' if domain == 'constant' else 'nonzero' if domain == 'nonzero' else 'zeros' if domain == 'zeros' else 'large' if domain == 'large' else 'subnormal' if domain == 'subnormal' else 'free'
derive.dom_lo: -0.01 if domain == 'narrow' else -8.0 if domain == 'wide' else 0.25 if domain == 'positive' else 0.5 if domain == 'constant' else -1.0
derive.dom_hi: 0.01 if domain == 'narrow' else 8.0 if domain == 'wide' else 4.0 if domain == 'positive' else 0.5 if domain == 'constant' else 1.0
derive.eff_placement: 'exact' if placement == 'under' and alignment < 2 else placement

constraints.reason: backward is a training-mode op, so N * spatial must be > 1 (frontend validateBatchNormTrainingSpatialDimensions via BatchnormBackwardNode.hpp:162; engine BatchnormValidator::checkBwdTensorConfigSupported passes isTraining=true to validateSpatialDimensions, BatchnormApplicabilityChecks.cpp:29,414-437)

oracle cost ceiling (RFC 0023 section 14), lower than the 2**30 normalization ceiling because the GPU graph executor has no BatchNorm backward plan (GpuReferenceGraphExecutor.hpp:189), so the scalar CPU reference (CpuFpReferenceBatchnorm.hpp:296-394, three passes per channel with an index vector per element) is the oracle; keeps the extents inside the kernel's int template parameters too (Configuration.hpp proto_config, BatchnormBwdPlan.cpp:248-253)

the special fill plants at least one non-finite element per tensor (FillInputs.cpp:494-498), so at c == 1 the only channel of scale is poisoned and every element of dx is non-finite; a reference with no finite element fails under match_nonfinite whatever the engine wrote (docs/file-formats.md, validator section: 'A reference with no finite element ... fails')

the half and bfloat16 dx tolerances are atol = rtol = 4e-4 and 3e-3 (TestTolerances.hpp:99-121 getToleranceBackward), below one ulp of the result once |dx| is above about 2.6 (half) or 1 (bfloat16); saved mean and inv_variance are literal ranges unrelated to x, so xhat * mean(xhat * dy) is not cancelled (CpuFpReferenceBatchnorm.hpp:372,390) and these domains give |dx| from a few units to thousands; the engine and the fp32 CPU reference round the reductions differently, so a few elements per thousand differ by exactly one ulp and fail (measured on gfx950, half and bfloat16 NHWC at alignment >= 4: the 7 wide, 2 positive and 5 large mismatches of two fuzz runs, seeds 5000..5063 and 7000..7159, all differ by exactly one ulp of the result, e.g. ref 2.535156 impl 2.537109 in half). float is graded at 2e-3 against an ulp of 1e-6 and keeps all domains. A TOML tolerance for these tensors would lift the constraint

the CPU reference sums dscale and dbias per channel as one sequential fp32 sum (CpuFpReferenceBatchnorm.hpp:353-367; ComputeDataType defaults to MeanVarianceDataType = float, :270-272); N equal terms stagnate once the ulp of the running sum reaches the term, a relative error of up to 2**-24 * N (emulated worst case over the dscale term range 0.38..0.6: 4.5e-4 at N = 32768, 9.7e-4 at 65536, doubling per doubling), against a dscale and dx tolerance of 2e-3; the engine's parallel reduction is the accurate side (measured on gfx950, seed s1020, N = 2198432: emulating the reference's sequential fp32 sum of the term implied by the engine's dscale reproduces the reference value to all printed digits, 1.129627e6 against the engine's 1.161032e6)

same sequential fp32 reference sum (CpuFpReferenceBatchnorm.hpp:353-367): for terms of one sign the sum passes 2**22 and rounds every add to a coarse grid, which biases it: emulating the sum of 4096000 uniform(0.25, 4) float terms gives +2.0e-3 against the exact sum, 2.4e-4 at 2**21 and 1.4e-5 or less up to 2**20, against a dbias tolerance of 2e-3 (measured on gfx950, seed s8135, float, N = 4096000: reference dbias 8.721585e6, engine 8.703704e6, expected N * mean(dy) = 8.704e6, so the engine is the accurate side)

constraints.rule: domain not in ['wide', 'large'] or n * hw <= 2**11
constraints.reason: dbias and dscale are sums of random-sign terms of magnitude 4.6 to 24 (wide, large), and the sequential fp32 reference sum (CpuFpReferenceBatchnorm.hpp:353-367) and the engine's tree reduction differ by about 1e-2 once the partial sums reach 1e4; a channel whose true sum lands near zero then misses atol 2e-3 + rtol * |ref| (measured on gfx950, float NHWC alignment 4, c = 256, 16 to 32 draws per size: 0 failures at n*hw <= 4096 for wide and at 2048 for large, then 3 to 17 percent of cases at n*hw = 4096 (large) to 32768, always one channel of dbias or dscale). A TOML rms validator for dscale and dbias, as LayernormBackward has, would lift the bound
